# Succajajātaka (Ja 320)

**ID:** Ja 320
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Succajajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

In the Pali commentary edited by V. Fausböll, it forms the twentieth story of the *Pucimandavagga* [Fausböll 1883]. The framing story is set at Jetavana and delivered by the Buddha regarding a certain landowner and his wife [Appleton 2010]. As Naomi Appleton observes, it is one of the infrequent instances where a laywoman forms the primary audience for a Jātaka; the Buddha recounts the tale to the landowner's wife after her husband shows ingratitude and lack of affection [Appleton 2010].

In the story of the past, a queen asks the king whether he would give her gold if the mountain before them were made of gold, to which he coldly replies that he would not [Ānandajoti 2010]. The verses emphasize that the wise recognize a person who boasts without acting (*akarontaṁ bhāsamānaṁ parijānanti paṇḍitā*) [Ānandajoti 2010]. According to the commentary's conclusion (*samodhāna*), the Bodhisatta was the wise minister (*paṇḍitāmacco*), while the King of Bārāṇasī and his queen were the landowner and his wife in that past life; upon hearing the teaching, the married couple attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1883].
